title: Rohan at the Louvre
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: As a teenager, manga artist Rohan Kishibe has a brief romance with a mysterious young widow who tells him of a cursed 200-year-old painting made with the blackest ink, taken from a sacred thousand-year-old tree the painter felled without the Emperor's permission, for which he was executed. Ten years later, famous, Rohan tracks the painting to the Louvre's storage archives, where the curse is unleashed on him and the museum staff. A single-volume, full-color horror story by JoJo's Bizarre Adventure creator Hirohiko Araki, made for the Louvre's comics collection.
life_message: Art carries the weight of the past, and some wrongs reach across generations.

content.note: Bodies twisting and bursting in red-and-black gore (ANN); Gore, Body Horror (AniList); Blood and Gore (MangaUpdates).
Ghost-story curse and haunting in the archives (ANN; AniList Ghost, MangaUpdates Haunting).
Teen Rohan's first love with an older widow (ANN, MangaUpdates First Love); no sexual content noted.
Curse driving people to harm (to verify).
Commissioned by Louvre Editions; spin-off of the JoJo franchise.

dominant: Art and obsession; inherited curse; gothic horror

frames.aligns: Consequences of sacrilege (felling a sacred tree) and of curiosity unchecked.
frames.concerns: Curse and haunting treated as real; graphic gore.

frames.aligns: Warning against prying into dark things.

frames.concerns: Curses and ghosts as open doors.

frames.aligns: Common-grace appreciation of art and the Louvre.

frames.concerns: Curses and spirits; images of living beings central.

frames.aligns: Karma of a sacrilegious act returning.

frames.concerns: Ghosts of the dead shown as real; horror.

frames.aligns: Sacred tree (shinboku) and tatari: a kami's curse for disrespect.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Painter's offense against the Emperor answered by execution and curse (NBM blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Rohan follows his curiosity alone, defying caution.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Imperial authority in backstory; modern Rohan independent.

folkways.japan: Draws on Japanese ghost-story (kaidan) tradition and the idea of tatari, a curse for violating a sacred tree.

delivery.evidence: ANN column calls the plot flimsy and focuses on visual style, with no stated message.
delivery.note: A ghost story told for style; any moral about art and the past is left to inference.

winners_losers: Rohan survives the curse; the museum staff do not fare as well; sympathy is with Rohan and the wronged painter.
to_verify: Not a one-shot conflict: AniList one-shot and NBM English edition are the same single volume.
